prediction:
THOUGHT: Postoperative fever on day 3 has a broad differential (atelectasis, pneumonia, wound infection, UTI, PE). Key findings point to a pulmonary infectious process: pleuritic right-sided chest pain, new productive cough, inspiratory crackles at the right base, elevated WBC, and a chest x-ray showing a right lower‑lobe infiltrate. Wound infection is unlikely given a soft, nontender abdomen and the early timing (usually later). Atelectasis commonly causes low‑grade fever early post‑op and may show volume loss rather than a focal infiltrate and is less likely to produce purulent sputum and leukocytosis. PE can cause pleuritic pain and fever but usually without a focal infiltrate or productive cough. Taken together the clinical picture and imaging are most consistent with an acute right lower‑lobe pneumonia occurring after surgery (postoperative pneumonia, likely aspiration-related). 
DIAGNOSIS: Postoperative right lower‑lobe pneumonia (acute lobar pneumonia)
